newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NCR expects higher revenues in 1997 - CEO.
newsitem.headline: NCR expects higher revenues in 1997 - CEO.

text.p: NCR Corp chairman Lars Nyberg said on Saturday he expected the company's total revenue in 1997 to be slightly higher than the US$7.0 billion achieved last year. "We expect some growth over last year," he told Reuters following a news conference. "I will not disclose the number this year but it's slightly higher than the number last year."
He said because of the stronger earnings projected, the amount spent on research and development (R&D) this year, which would be about 6.5 percent of total revenue, would also be higher.
NCR spent some $450 million on R&D in 1996, said Nyberg, who is also the company's chief executive officer.

NCR, founded more than 100 years ago as National Cash Register, is the number one maker of automated teller machines (ATMs) and price scanners used in supermarkets and mass merchandise stores, he said. It is the number two maker of retail checkout point-of-sale systems.
NCR came under the stable of U.S. telecommunications giant AT&T Corp between 1991 and December 1996. Nyberg was the principal architect in the turnaround of NCR when it broke away from AT&T.
Nyberg told the news conference that the Internet or Intranet will fundamentally change the way NCR does its retail and banking business "as it will change the rules of the game."
"Therefore it will dramatically change the way NCR does its business."

He said in 1996 NCR was doing a vital turnaround for its survival. "So we started five to six months ago putting some real money and real efforts in providing solutions for our customers in the retail business and the financial business in the area of Internet technology," he said.
"I'm the first to admit that I would have liked NCR to be the inventor of it (Internet technology) and not so much the follower. We have to catch here...You bet we are going to catch up."
He said NCR has the ability to apply its technical knowledge of the Internet and Intranet to help its customers transform the way they do business.
